outcome: The question of whether there exists a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω (equivalently, whether ℵ_ω fails to be a Jónsson cardinal) remains open; no consistency result, proof, or refutation was found in the window, and the closest recent work (Rinot's 2023/2025-26 survey and related 2024-2026 papers) explicitly treats it, or the closely related successor-of-a-singular-cardinal version, as still unresolved.
summary: The problem asks whether ℵ_ω (the least possible Jónsson cardinal, since AC rules out any ℵ_n being Jónsson) admits a Jónsson algebra, i.e. whether ℵ_ω is 'not Jónsson'. I searched arXiv, Wikipedia's Jónsson cardinal article, Rinot's blog, and general web search for any resolution, partial case, or bound moved since 26 January 2024, and found none. The most relevant recent item is Assaf Rinot's survey 'May the successor of a singular cardinal be Jónsson?' (arXiv:2312.08253, submitted 13 Dec 2023 — before the window — and later published in the Bollettino dell'Unione Matematica Italiana, 2025-2026), which is explicitly a survey collecting necessary conditions for an affirmative answer and states the problem is still open; it concerns the successor of a singular cardinal (e.g. ℵ_{ω+1}), a related but distinct question from whether ℵ_ω itself is Jónsson, and in any case predates the window and contains no new theorem resolving either question. Other papers found while searching (Eskew–Hayut 'Dense ideals', Oct 2024; Inamdar–Rinot's club-guessing survey published Jan 2025; Poveda–Thei 'A Solovay-like model at ℵ_ω', Sep 2025/Jun 2026) are all in the surrounding area of singular-cardinal combinatorics but none address or settle the ℵ_ω-Jónsson question itself — Dense ideals is about dense ideals on successors of regular cardinals, the club-guessing survey is a general methods paper only listing Jónsson-algebra construction as one of many applications of club guessing, and the Solovay-like-model paper does not mention Jónsson algebras at all. No arXiv preprint, journal paper, or blog post from after 26 January 2024 was found claiming any progress — positive or negative — on the existence of a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω specifically. No AI system appears anywhere in this search: none of the papers found mention any AI, machine-learning, or automated-theorem-proving tool in their methodology.
competing_reading: One could argue the Rinot survey's 2025/2026 journal publication constitutes an 'event' in the window, since the written argument was substantially the same as the Dec 2023 preprint (I could not access the full text to confirm no additions), but per §6.3 dating goes by the first written argument (Dec 2023, before the window), and per §6.1 a survey restating an open problem is not itself an event that changes the status. It is also conceivable that the survey, being about the successor of a singular cardinal rather than ℵ_ω itself, is a related-but-distinct problem under §3.1's scope rule, in which case it is irrelevant to this record either way.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or paper proving either that ℵ_ω admits a Jónsson algebra (i.e., ℵ_ω is not Jónsson, provable outright in ZFC by generalizing Shelah's ℵ_{ω+1} argument or similar), or establishing/refuting the consistency of ℵ_ω being Jónsson relative to some large cardinal hypothesis (e.g., resolving the generic I0 consistency question), dated after 26 January 2024, with an expert digestion or journal acceptance.
